name: Methimazole

fda.text: First Trimester Use of Methimazole and Congenital Malformations Methimazole crosses the placental membranes and can cause fetal harm when administered in the first trimester of pregnancy. Rare instances of congenital defects, including aplasia cutis, craniofacial malformations (facial dysmorphism; choanal atresia),…

summary: A warning states that Methimazole can pass into the placenta and harm an unborn baby if taken during the first three months of pregnancy [3]. It has been linked to rare birth defects, such as missing skin (aplasia cutis) and abnormalities of the head or face [3]. In addition, a small computer model rather than human testing estimated a medium score for liver concerns and a low score for heart concerns [M].
